prerequisites: Solid prior knowledge in mathematics (differential equations, linearization, Laplace transform, complex numbers)
Basic knowledge from mechanics, electrical engineering, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics
Successful completion of the StEOP (Study Introduction and Orientation Phase)

learning_outcomes.text: Name basic signal parameters, fundamental metrological and device-specific terms, and typical measurement errors.
Describe the structure, function, and application areas of central measuring instruments (measuring amplifiers, display and recording devices, oscilloscopes).
Perform simple measurement tasks including laboratory measurements, data acquisition and protocol creation, graphical representation, and basic error calculation.
Analyze mechanical vibration systems (linear one and multi-degree-of-freedom systems) in the context of measurement systems and machine setups.
Explain fundamental control engineering terms, system descriptions, and modeling approaches.
Formulate linear control engineering models of technical systems in the time and frequency domains.
Investigate the dynamic behavior of systems using transfer functions, block diagrams, and frequency response curves.
Design PID controllers based on given time or frequency domain specifications.
Assess the stability of closed-loop control systems using suitable criteria.
Transfer acquired methodological knowledge to further tasks and courses in control engineering.
Recognize interdependencies and couplings of systems and derive courses of action for controlling, regulating, and optimizing technical processes.
Present correlations in a structured and audience-appropriate manner.
Work cooperatively on problems in a team and take responsibility.
Increasingly independently plan workflows in exercise and laboratory environments.
Critically compare and evaluate information from different sources.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of Measurement Technology: Signal parameters, measurement errors, measuring instruments and measuring amplifiers
Fundamentals of Vibration Technology: SDOF vibrators, linear torsional vibrators, vibration isolation
Execution and evaluation of measurement exercises including error calculation
Execution of measurement exercises with protocol creation
Fundamentals of Control Engineering: Terms, system descriptions and model building
Linearization, transfer functions and block diagrams
Analysis of dynamic systems in the time and frequency domain (frequency response, Nyquist plot, Bode diagram)
Classification of transfer behavior, dead-time and all-pass systems
Controller design with PID controllers and stability analysis of closed-loop control systems
teaching_methods: Inverted-classroom elements with preparatory learning materials for independent content acquisition
Face-to-face and online live sessions for content deepening
Independent study of selected content using current scientific literature

assessment_methods.method: Written and/or oral examination on theoretical fundamentals
Presentation and documentation of independently developed solutions to automation and control engineering problems
Active participation in the measurement experiment (Measurement Technology Lab)
